title: Heterogeneous programming-model fragmentation
bottleneck: GPUs, TPUs, NPUs, and emerging accelerators each demand their own programming model and toolchain, with CUDA's moat keeping most AI development NVIDIA-bound. Portable frameworks (OpenCL, SYCL, Triton) lag in performance and library coverage, so code written for one accelerator rarely runs well on another. Hardware innovation outpaces software portability.
why_it_blocks: Fragmentation slows the adoption of better or cheaper accelerators: developers won't target hardware their code can't reach. It entrenches incumbents, raises costs, and means much of the world's accelerator innovation can't be used by mainstream developers.
current_state: Triton, MLIR-based compilers, and open standards are improving portability, and some non-NVIDIA accelerators gain traction. CUDA's ecosystem lead remains decisive in practice. Library coverage is the real moat: even when alternative compilers match individual kernels, they lack the decade of tuned primitives that incumbents ship.
